content.text: All handle names are valid. Let me validate the JSON:

The fix is complete. Here's what was wrong.

## What was broken

The map was blank because of **two independent bugs**, either of which alone would have hidden the earthquake points:

### 1. The layer was never connected to the renderer (primary cause)
The graph built a `ScatterplotLayer` and wired up all its inputs (data, position, radius, color), but **no edge fed that layer into the `DeckRenderer`'s `layers` input**. The only thing connected to `/deck` was the basemap. So deck.gl rendered the map with zero layers — a blank map.

I added the missing edge:
```
/scatterplot-layer.out.layer → /deck.par.layers
```

### 2. Wrong column-name case in the position accessor
The CSV headers are capitalized (`Latitude`, `Longitude`, `Magnitude`), but the position accessor read lowercase fields:
```js
[d.longitude, d.latitude]   // both undefined → NaN positions
```
Even once the layer was connected, every point would have had an invalid `[undefined, undefined]` position and drawn nothing. I fixed it to:
```js
[d.Longitude, d.Latitude]
```

(The magnitude accessor already correctly used `d.Magnitude`, which is why only position was affected.)

Everything else checked out — the `MapRange → ColorRamp` color chain, the `sqrt`/`multiply` radius math, and all the handle names are valid. With both fixes in place the earthquake points will render, sized by magnitude and colored via the turbo ramp.

### 1. The layer was never connected to the renderer (primary cause)
